summary: Recurrent checkpoint restores no longer recompute a prompt because a rank's transfer worker rejected an admitted copy
details: The recurrent checkpoint bridge admits up to 32 stores and restores at a time, but each TP rank's transfer worker was created with room for 16. Under copy pressure a healthy worker rejected a copy the scheduler had already admitted; the connector reported it as a miss, a restore spent another lookup attempt and could end up recomputing its prompt without reading the payload on that rank.

Each rank's worker now admits 34 copies (the 32 the scheduler can hand it plus one completed job per copy thread whose permit is released a moment after its result is visible), with two copy threads as before.
Six CPU regressions exercise admission of the full scheduler allowance on both ranks with delayed completion callbacks.
